result.title: FinGREAT: Evaluating LLMs on Financial Graph-guided Retrieval And Typing
result.summary: Financial disclosures express the underlying relationships of double-entry accounting through unstructured text. While financial LLM benchmarks predominantly emphasize question answering and classification, schema-guided evidence discovery remains relatively under-explored. We investigate whether open-weight LLMs can extract and classify evidence corresponding to predefined double-entry accounting relationships underlying the text. Using a financial accounting graph comprising 11 nodes (accounts) and 11 edges (transaction types), we evaluate mid-sized models from 5 open-weight families across 1,300 SEC 10-K Item 7 filings spanning 26 years, comparing their extraction performance against three proprietary models. Results reveal substantial differences in extraction volume, edge distributions, and cross-model agreement. Building on this study, we introduce a human-annotated relation classification benchmark comprising 483 passages across three financial accounting categories, evaluating 34 open-weight and 10 proprietary models. The strongest open-weight and proprietary models achieve 84.1\% and 92.8\% accuracy, respectively, with considerable variation across accounting categories. Our findings highlight the importance of evaluating evidence discovery and relation understanding separately, while investigating locally deployable models for scalable, privacy-sensitive financial analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文构建金融披露领域的图结构评测：用 11 账户节点、11 交易类型边构成的复式记账图，考察开放权重与专有 LLM 从 SEC 10-K 文本中抽取并分类证据关系的能力，并发布 483 段人工标注的关系分类基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于金融文本领域的抽取与关系分类基准，既不涉及 latent 推理状态、视觉证据筛选，也没有生成、训练监督或停止决策方面的机制，仅「schema 引导的证据发现」一词与 LVR 表面相似，缺乏可供核查的具体迁移线索。
